description: Clean structured catalog of ECCD Checklist domains and items for BrightSteps rule-based developmental progress engine. Derived from official ECCD Checklist Child's Record 1 (0–36 months) and Record 2 (older children). Titles cleaned for digital encoding; original procedures/materials remain in the paper instrument.

record1.label: ECCD Checklist – Child’s Record 1
record1.recommended_frequency: Every 4 months (0–12 mo); every 6 months (13–36 mo)

GM.title: Infant lifts head when held standing
GM.procedure: Hold the child in an upright position and carefully remove your hand from the child’s neck according to his ability to lift his head and keep it erect. Credit if the child occasionally lifts his head free of support. Parental report will suffice.

GM.title: Infant tries to lift head when lying on stomach
GM.procedure: Place the child on his stomach on a flat stomach surface. Credit if the child at least momentarily lifts his head so that the chin is off the surface. Parental report will suffice.

GM.title: Infant holds head upright on his own when lying on stomach
GM.procedure: Place the child on his stomach on a flat when lying on surface. Credit if the child lifts his head stomach and chest up so that his face makes a 90° angle w/ the surface for at least several seconds. Parental report will suffice.

GM.title: Infant holds head steadily
GM.procedure: Parental report will suffice.

GM.title: Infant rolls over from back to stomach with assistance
GM.procedure: Place the child on his back on a flat surface. stomach with Encourage him to roll over to his stomach, assistance providing some assistance to do so. Credit if he eventually rolls over. Parental report will suffice.

GM.title: Infant turns from side to back without assistance
GM.procedure: Roll the child from his back to his side. without assistance Make sure he is not restricted by his clothes and his arm is not caught under his torso. Credit if the child actively turns from his side to his back. Parental report will suffice.

GM.title: Infant sits well with support, leaning on hands
GM.procedure: Hold the child in a sitting position on the hands if placed on table and slowly remove your hand from the hard surface child making sure that he does not fall. Credit if the child sits alone and puts his hands on his legs or on the table for support. Parental report will suffice.

GM.title: Infant bounces when held standing, briefly bearing weight on legs
GM.procedure: Parental report will suffice.

GM.title: Infant sits alone steadily
GM.procedure: Hold the child in a sitting position on the table and slowly remove your hand from him making sure that he does not fall. Credit if the child sits alone steadily without support, keeping his back fairly straight. Parental report will suffice.

GM.title: Infant moves from sitting to creeping/crawling position
GM.procedure: Seat the child on the floor. Place a toy on the floor, in front of the child, but not within his reach. Observe how the child moves from sitting to creeping position and the type of movement he makes to reach for the toy. Credit if the child moves forward about 9 inches or more, using either of the following: hands and knees, stomach and arms, hands and feet. Parental report will suffice.

GM.title: Infant pulls self from sitting to standing with minimal assistance
GM.procedure: With the child in a sitting position, hold standing position both his hands and have him pull himself with minimal up with only minimal assistance from the assistance adult. Credit if the child can stand up. Parental report will suffice.

GM.title: Stands with minimum support
GM.procedure: Credit if the child holds on to a piece of furniture with both hands and bears weight on both feet. Parental report will suffice. B. Optional starting point for children aged 1 year 1 month - 3.0 years Gross Motor Material/Procedure Present Comments

GM.title: Holds furniture with both hands and walks sideways
GM.procedure: walks sideways While the child is standing, observe if he moves from one point to another by walking sideways. He may support himself by holding on to furniture. He can be encouraged to walk by placing a toy on the furniture near the child but just outside his reach so he must walk to reach the toy. Credit if the child walks sideways while holding on to furniture for support and balance. Parental report will suffice.

GM.title: Walks with both hands held
GM.procedure: Observe the child if he walks when both hands are held by an adult. Credit if the child takes coordinated walking steps with only slight support from the adult. Parental report will suffice.

GM.title: Climbs on chair or elevated furniture without help
GM.procedure: Parental report will suffice.

GM.title: Walks alone, rarely falls
GM.procedure: Observe the child if he walks alone across the room. Credit if the child walks alone with good balance without tripping and rarely falling. Parental report will suffice.

GM.title: Walks backwards
GM.procedure: Ask the child to walk backwards by demonstrating it. Credit if the child is able to walk backwards without falling and holding on to anything. Parental report will suffice.

GM.title: Runs without tripping or falling
GM.procedure: Credit if the child can run fast and smoothly without tripping or falling.

GM.title: Walks down stairs, 2 feet on each step, with one hand held
GM.procedure: Parental report will suffice.

GM.title: Walks up stairs holding handrail, 2 feet on each step
GM.procedure: feet on each step Place a toy in the middle of the step and ask the child to walk up the stairs to get the toy. Credit if the child walks up the stairs using the handrail or wall for support and places both feet on each step before stepping on the next one. Parental report will suffice.

GM.title: Walks upstairs with alternate feet without holding handrail
GM.procedure: without holding on Place a toy in the middle of the step and to the handrail ask the child to walk upstairs to get the toy. Credit if the child walks upstairs, alternating his feet as he steps on each successive step without holding on to the handrail or wall for support. Parental report will suffice.

GM.title: Walks downstairs without holding onto a handrail
GM.procedure: without holding Place a toy at the bottom of the stairs and onto a handrail ask the child to walk downstairs to get the toy. Credit if the child walks downstairs, alternating his feet as he steps on each successive step without holding on to the handrail or wall for support. Do not give credit if the child places both feet on the step or uses the handrail or wall for support. Parental report will suffice.

FM.procedure: Seat the child on the parent’s lap with his elbows at level with the tabletop and his hands on the table or flat surface. Drop a small toy in front of him and attract his attention by pointing to the toy or tapping the table/flat surface. Credit if the child picks up the toy, using all five fingers as if raking.

FM.title: Displays a definite hand preference
FM.procedure: Place the toy directly in front of the child at midline (not to his left or his right) and ask him to reach for this. Credit if he uses the same hand two out of three times. Parental report will suffice.

FM.title: Grasps and transfers small objects using neat pincer grasp
FM.procedure: Observe if the child transfers a small toy from one hand to the other. Encourage this by giving the child a toy and then present- ing another toy to the same hand. Credit if the child transfers a toy from one hand to the other without using his mouth or body.

RL.title: Infant startles to loud sounds
RL.procedure: Parental report will suffice.

RL.title: Infant turns eyes/head toward sound of rattle or voice
RL.procedure: Carry the child on his back with one hand and with the other shake a rattle out of his range of vision 6 inches from his ear. Do this continuously for 3 seconds and observe whether he can turn towards the sound. Credit if the child widens or moves his eyes from side to side in search of the sound.

RL.title: Understands 'no' / 'don't'
RL.procedure: Shake your head and finger and say “No-no”. Then see whether the child understands this. Credit if the child stops what he is doing. Parental report will suffice.

RL.title: Imitates adults' gestures (bye-bye, clap)
RL.procedure: Place the child on the playful sounds like caregiver’s lap with you facing the child. coughing, lip Then make the following sounds: cough, smacking smack lips. Credit if the child makes the same sound or even just the lip movements.

RL.title: Follows one-step command with gesture
RL.procedure: With the child seated in front of you, give used him a spoon then ask for the spoon back by saying “GIVE ME THE _(object)__.” with your hand (palm up) toward him. Credit if the child looks at the object and hands it over to you even if he does not release this immediately. Receptive Language Material/Procedure Present Comments

RL.title: Follows one-step command without gestures
RL.procedure: Place the toy on the floor and ask the child to pick this up without pointing to the toy or using any other gesture. Credit if the child picks up the toy.

RL.title: Points to five body parts when named
RL.procedure: Have the child point to his eyes, nose, when asked to do mouth, hands and feet. Credit if he can so point to all these.

RL.title: Points to five common objects when named
RL.procedure: Show the child a picture book (two to do so pictures per page) and ask him to point to the picture by saying “Where’s the ______?” Credit if the child can use his finger to point to at least five pictures.

RL.title: Follows one-step command involving an object
RL.procedure: Ask the child to put a block/toy under the prepositions (e.g., table; on the table; in the bag. Do not in, on, under, etc.) point or use gestures when giving the instruction. Credit if the child is able to follow at least one of the instructions.

RL.title: Follows two-step related commands
RL.procedure: Ask the child to get a block/toy from prepositions under the table and then place it on the table. Do not point or use gestures when giving the instruction. Credit if the child is able to follow.

COG.procedure: With the child seated, get his attention and drop a spoon/ball in front of him. Then observe if his eyes look down as the object falls. Credit if the child can bring his eyes and head down as the object falls.

COG.title: Looks for a partially hidden object
COG.procedure: With the child facing you, partially hide a ball behind a small towel and observe if he will look for it and find it. Credit if the child pulls the towel and gets the hidden ball.

COG.title: Matches objects

FM.title: Scribbles vertical and horizontal lines
FM.procedure: Place a piece paper and pencil/crayon on the table or flat surface and ask the child to draw vertical and horizontal lines after you have demonstrated these to him. Credit if the child produces a vertical or horizontal line that is at least 2 inches long and does not deviate or vary from your vertical line by more than 30 degrees. The lines may be wavy but not broken.

FM.title: Draws circle purposefully
FM.procedure: Place a paper and pencil/crayon on the table or flat surface and ask the child to draw a circle or a ball after you have demonstrated it to him. Credit if the child produces any curve that is closed or nearly closed. Continuous spiral motions are not credited.

FM.title: Draws a human figure
FM.procedure: Give the child a pencil and a paper and ask him to draw a picture of a person. Credit if the child has drawn three or more body parts. A pair is considered one part (eyes, ears, arms, hands, legs, and feet) and must be drawn in pairs to get full credit unless the drawing is in profile.

FM.title: Draws a house using basic shapes
FM.procedure: Give the child a pencil and paper and ask him to draw a picture of a house. Credit if the child has drawn at least the roof, main frame, and a door or window.
